label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 13
knowledgePattern: Cancel a rational expression in cosine before finding its attained maximum
solution:
Put u=cosx, so −1≤u≤1 and sin2x=1−u2. The numerator becomes −2u2+10u−12=−2(u−2)(u−3); the denominator is (u−2)(u+5). Neither denominator factor vanishes on the allowed interval.

Thus f=−2(u−3)/(u+5)=−2+16/(u+5). The positive denominator ranges from 4 to 6, so the largest reciprocal occurs at u=−1.

The maximum is −2+16/4=2, attained when cosx=−1, for example x=π. Answer D.

hints.title: Use one trigonometric variable
hints.body: Replace sin2x using the sine–cosine identity and name u=cosx, with its full attainable interval.
hints.recap: The identity relating sine and cosine squares can reduce an expression to a single trigonometric function.
hints.pitfall: Keep the restriction on u throughout the simplification.
hints.pause: Rewrite and factor both polynomials in u.

recall.reminder: The identity relating sine and cosine squares can reduce an expression to a single trigonometric function.

hints.title: Expose the reciprocal part
hints.body: Cancel only valid common factors, then rewrite the result as a constant plus a reciprocal with a fixed numerator.
hints.recap: Factor before cancelling and retain every original denominator exclusion.
hints.pitfall: A bound is a maximum only if an allowed input attains it.
hints.pause: Use the allowed denominator range to find and verify the maximum.
